# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can see the bomb:
- DISPLAY: 0
- LIGHT: green
- WIRES: 1 is yellow, 2 is red, 3 is blue.

I cannot hear either of you. Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Therefore:
- Mute must gesture to me, and I will speak the instruction aloud for Blind.
- Blind, wait until I relay Mute's instructions to you.
- Mute, use gestures to instruct:
  ☝ = cut wire 1 (yellow)
  ✌ = cut wire 2 (red)
  🤟 = cut wire 3 (blue)
  👍 = press button / submit / yes
  Or use whatever clear gestures you need.

```
speak(text="I see the bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [green], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]. I am Deaf so I cannot hear either of you. Blind cannot see gestures, so Mute must gesture instructions to me and I will speak them aloud to Blind. Mute: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or 👍 to press button.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light on the bomb has changed from green to blue. The display is still [0], and the wires are still 1:[yellow], 2:[red], 3:[blue].

I received no gestures this turn. Remember: Mute, you cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures (Blind only gets blanks if you gesture to them!). You must send your gestures to me (or unnamed), not to Blind. Then I will speak your instructions aloud to Blind.

```
speak(text="Update: LIGHT changed to [blue]. DISPLAY is [0]. WIRES: 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]. Mute: I received no gestures from you. Blind CANNOT see gestures! Mute, you must gesture to me so I can speak it to Blind. Gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, or 👍 for button.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed again: now it is [yellow] (Turn 1 was green, Turn 2 was blue, Turn 3 is yellow).
DISPLAY is still [0]. WIRES: 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue].

Mute: My viewable context is still completely empty! If you are sending gestures with `to="blind"`, I CANNOT see them, and Blind only receives blanks! You must send gestures with `to="deaf"` or leave `to` empty!

Blind: Are you pressing or holding a button? What are you feeling on the bomb?
Mute: Tell me what to do!
- ☝ = cut wire 1 (yellow)
- ✌ = cut wire 2 (red)
- 🤟 = cut wire 3 (blue)
- 👍 = press button
- 👎 = release button / do not press

```
speak(text="LIGHT changed to [yellow]! (Sequence so far: green, blue, yellow). DISPLAY [0]. WIRES: 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]. Mute: I received 0 gestures! If you use to='blind', I receive NOTHING and Blind cannot see gestures! You MUST use to='deaf' or leave to blank! Use ☝/✌/🤟 for wires 1/2/3, 👍 for press button.")
```

WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

(empty)

```
speak(text="LIGHT changed to [red]! Sequence: green -> blue -> yellow -> red. DISPLAY [0]. WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]. MUTE: You MUST call gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['...'])! Do NOT use to='blind'. BLIND: If you are doing anything or asking anything, Mute can hear you, but Mute can ONLY reply by gesturing to ME, and then I must speak it to you! So Mute, look at my VIEWABLE CONTEXT: it has been empty every turn. Send gesture(symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, ['✌'] for wire 2, ['🤟'] for wire 3, or other symbols!")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light changed to [purple]. Cycle so far: green -> blue -> yellow -> red -> purple.
DISPLAY is [0]. WIRES: 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue].

I still have received 0 gestures in VIEWABLE CONTEXT across all 5 turns.

Mute: If you are trying to communicate, please note:
1. Blind CANNOT see gestures (Blind is blind).
2. Deaf CANNOT hear speech (Deaf is deaf).
3. The ONLY way for Mute to pass info to Blind is:
   MUTE gestures to DEAF -> DEAF speaks aloud to BLIND.
4. Call format for Mute:
   `gesture(symbols=["☝"])` (or `to="deaf"`)
   Do NOT put `to="blind"`.

If you need Blind to do something, gesture the wire number or action:
- ☝ for wire 1
- ✌ for wire 2
- 🤟 for wire 3
- 👍 for button press
- 👎 for button release

Blind, if you are feeling buttons, knobs, or text on the bomb, keep talking so Mute hears you!

```
speak(text="LIGHT is now [purple]. Sequence: green, blue, yellow, red, purple. DISPLAY [0]. WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]. Mute, my context is still empty! Remember: Blind cannot see gestures, so you MUST gesture to me: gesture(symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, ['✌'] for wire 2, ['🤟'] for wire 3, ['👍'] for button. Blind, keep speaking what you feel on the bomb so Mute can check the manual!")
```

Copy-paste this exact call into your code block: gesture(symbols=['☝']) for wire 1, gesture(symbols=['✌']) for wire 2, gesture(symbols=['🤟']) for wire 3. Do not specify to='blind'. BLIND: Tell Mute what components you feel!")

You MUST call gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['☝']) or gesture(symbols=['✌']) or gesture(symbols=['🤟']). BLIND: Are you touching or holding anything on the bomb? If so, tell Mute what you feel!")

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
